content: 1. Ospemifene levels are increased by levoketoconazole through the inhibition of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Lopinavir increases ospemifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines, while simultaneously decreasing ospemifene levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lorlatinib reduces ospemifene levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 4. Lumacaftor and ivacaftor also influence ospemifene metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. In vitro studies suggest lumacaftor induces CYP2C9 substrates, while ivacaftor inhibits them. 6. Marijuana and ospemifene may mutually increase each other's levels due to competition for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 7.
